items.description: Mount Manengouba is a majestic extinct volcano featuring unique twin crater lakes known as the 'Male' and 'Female' lakes.
The Nkam Basin is a fertile valley and river system known for its lush vegetation and rich agricultural potential in the Littoral Region.
The coastal forests of Kribi are a lush tropical paradise where the jungle meets the sandy shores of the Atlantic Ocean.
The montane forests surrounding Buea are part of the Mount Cameroon ecosystem, home to rare plants and a variety of bird species.
The marshlands around Kribi are important coastal wetlands that support a variety of aquatic life and migratory bird species.
The Mungo marshes are expansive wetlands in the Littoral Region, providing a critical habitat for diverse flora and fauna.
The Mandara Mountains are a dramatic volcanic range in the Far North, known for their rugged beauty and unique terrace farming.
The relief of Mount Manengouba is defined by its massive caldera and the lush, rolling grasslands of the highland plateau.
Mount Kupe is a significant peak in the Bakossi mountain range, rising steeply from the surrounding tropical forests.
Mount Oissa is a notable elevation in central Cameroon, contributing to the varied and hilly topography of the region.
The Nlonako Mountains are part of Cameroon's western volcanic line, featuring dense forests and significant biodiversity.
Mount Bambouto is a massive volcanic complex in the West Region, forming part of the Cameroon Highlands.
Mount Tchabal Mbabo is one of the highest peaks in the Adamawa Region, offering rugged terrain and panoramic views of the plateau.
The Rumpi Hills are a volcanic mountain range in the Southwest Region, known for their steep slopes and dense tropical forests.
Mount Ntem is a prominent elevation in the South Region, characterized by its dense rainforest cover and rolling hills.
